hypothesis_tested: `692` is a hard terminal selector under `002-390`, but its global behavior may be driven by a portable `060-692` suffix.

family_rows.parse_implication: `692` is strict-source local evidence for a terminal branch under `002-390`, but the family has one known row.
`060-692` is the dominant portable terminal suffix ecology; it can explain much of global 692 terminality.
Even outside `060-692`, the sign remains often terminal, but much less cleanly than the dominant suffix family.

decisions.named_bet: `692` is a hard terminal closure selector under `002-390`
decisions.evidence: Canonical 692 has 68 occurrences and 50 are terminal; the one 002-390-692 row is terminal.
decisions.adversary: Dominant 060-692 accounts for 39/68 canonical occurrences and 33/39 are terminal, so global closure is partly a suffix-family effect.
decisions.falsifier_or_rescue: A source-bound 002-390-692 continuation kills the local terminal selector. A second strict 002-390-692 terminal row outside the 060 family promotes the branch rule.

decisions.named_bet: `060-692` is a portable terminal suffix and `390-692` borrows its final closure element
decisions.evidence: 060 is the top predecessor of 692: 39/68; terminal after 060 is 33/39.
decisions.adversary: `390-692` has no visible `060`; the borrowing/stripping story is a semantic bridge, not directly observed morphology.
decisions.falsifier_or_rescue: If 060-692 source-normalizes to a narrow copied family, this demotes. If independent sites/forms preserve 060-692 terminality, keep it as a suffix candidate.

decisions.named_bet: `692` is just an ordinary sign whose terminality is accidental
decisions.evidence: Among 23 count-matched signs including 692, it ranks 1/23 by terminal share.
decisions.adversary: Count matching does not control for inherited formula families, so this only attacks the lazy accidental-terminal null.
decisions.falsifier_or_rescue: If count-matched signs routinely show the same terminal share once formula-collapsed, ordinary-sign null revives.
